manifests.summary: SECOND RESEARCH PASS (first since 2026-06-16). Extends the claimed layer with the actual published Challenger figures for June, July and August 2026 (YTD Jan–Aug reconciles exactly: 529,914 total / 116,175 AI; no revisions to Jan–May). AI-cited cuts peaked in May (38,579, 40% of the month), held near a third of cuts in June (14,029) and July (10,970), then fell to 3,462 in August (6.5%) — the first month since February AI did not lead. JOLTS re-pulled through July 2026 (BLS revised April; see JOLTS). Adds 27 new events for 2026-06-01 → 2026-09-18 (8 B1 where the company itself cited AI — all mixed-cause or floor-counted, 3 B2, 6 B3, 10 B0 baseline) and 17 corrections to the June ledger, chiefly SEC-filing corroborations (A2→A1) plus two revised counts (Cloudflare ~1,100; Estée Lauder ~10,000), an Oracle B2→B1 on its 10-K language, and an Intel downgrade to A3. Every B-tier remains flagged for Jacob's review.
manifests.analyst: Phase-1 agent (Claude) — three parallel research agents (Challenger reports; AI-attributed events; baseline events + corrections + context). Seam verification by the orchestrating session, re-fetching primary sources directly on 2026-09-18: Rackspace 8-K (EDGAR: 'realign its workforce around how production AI is deployed…', ~15%, approved 2026-06-10) ✓; Visa (American Banker: CEO ties the 7% / ~2,600 cut to AI reshaping how work gets done) ✓; GitLab CEO post ('If an agent can do it, we automate it'; workforce reduction driven by country footprint) ✓; Microsoft company post (Amy Coleman: ~4,800 roles, 2.1%; 'the roles eliminated today are not being replaced by AI') ✓ — which is why Microsoft is held at B3 despite AI-driven headlines.
